original_test_intent: Verify that the exact firmware image intended for the target platform has the MD5 checksum published in its trusted release note before any separate flash action.
original_method: Bind and preserve the operator-selected firmware file, target/version and release note, reject an unstable or ambiguous path, compute MD5 read-only, compare the full value exactly and record stronger hash/signature evidence when available.
manual_activity: Owner identifies the exact immutable firmware image, intended target/version and trusted release-note MD5; this row does not include the duplicate F1 General Help action or any flash.
required_inputs: Exact firmware image path and immutable file metadata
Trusted release note/manifest and expected MD5
Artifact provenance and protected evidence storage
safety_requirements: Reject directories, mutable inputs and ambiguous symlinks
Hash only; do not execute, mount, modify or flash the file
Verify expected-value provenance and target mapping
Use MD5 as the source criterion but preserve stronger evidence when available
Do not clear logs or open BIOS General Help
agent_execution_scope: Resolve the exact trusted expected value
Compute full MD5 and SHA-256 read-only
engineer_actions: Supply and approve the intended artifact/target/version
Resolve any hash or signature mismatch
Own downstream flash approval and final verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `md5sum ${FW_IMAGE:?...}` directly tests the row's checksum criterion once the operator supplies the exact file, but a bare YES classification does not capture the necessary package and expected-value inputs; the General Help log instruction belongs to duplicate row 357.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After pinning a regular immutable firmware file and trusted release-note value, run md5sum and SHA-256/signature verification read-only, preserve full output and compare exact values without flashing or modifying the artifact.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: MD5 comparison to the release note and 10/10-minute timing are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture file identity before/after hashing, compare MD5 byte-for-byte to an independently trusted manifest and add SHA-256/signature evidence without changing acceptance semantics.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds provenance, input stability, target binding and modern integrity evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects wrong-file selection and manifest/signature disagreement that a naked MD5 line can miss.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: MD5 is not an authenticity guarantee and a matching hash for the wrong target remains operationally unsafe.

project_override_considerations: Project must provide the exact trusted release-note value and target/image mapping; no code-only lookup or duplicate F1 instruction may select the artifact.
expected_evidence: Full md5sum output and exact comparison
No flash or BIOS UI action
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure, Criteria and private checksum Script consistently target a firmware-file MD5 comparison. The duplicate-code General Help text is isolated as an erroneous DeepSeek log-output reference rather than an ambiguity in the primary row.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The purpose and command are clear; the firmware file, expected value and owner selection are finite package/user prerequisites.

review_improvement: Turns a path-only MD5 call into target-bound, provenance-preserving checksum evidence and prevents the duplicate BIOS help action from contaminating execution.
independent_technical_reasoning: Hashing is low-risk and automatable, but there is nothing valid to hash or compare until the owner supplies the exact image and independently trusted MD5 for its target/version. That material prerequisite changes DeepSeek's unconditional YES to REQUIRES.
